subject: Holloway Health — MSA/Order Form: IP & training clarifications
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@hollowayhealth.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@hollowayhealth.com
Date: Thu, 9 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Holloway — MSA/Order Form: IP and training questions

Hi Dev / Laura,

Thanks for the draft Order Form and MSA. Our legal team (cc'ed) reviewed and flagged two items we need clarity on before we proceed:

1) Output ownership — the current language in Exhibit A appears to grant Redwood rights to use customer outputs for productization. We need confirmation that Holloway retains exclusive rights to customer-generated outputs and that Redwood will not claim title or re-sell customer outputs.

2) Training / feedback license — our counsel is uncomfortable with any blanket right to train models on customer content. We can consider a narrow feedback license for non-customer-specific telemetry or aggregated signals, and an explicit opt-in for any use of raw customer content for model training.

Can you confirm Redwood's position and share any suggested redline language? If helpful, we can jump on a quick call; we aim to finalize the Order Form this week.

Also, please provide SOC2 evidence or a link to your compliance package and an outline of your data retention & deletion process for customer data.

Best,
Sophie Turner
Procurement Manager | Holloway Health
Sophie.Turner@hollowayhealth.com
Phone: (415) 555-0123

-----
Holloway Health — contracts@hollowayhealth.com

From: dev_patel@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 9 May 2028 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Holloway — MSA/Order Form: IP and training questions

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear note.

Quick answers up front:
- Output ownership: Redwood's standard is that customers keep ownership of their outputs; we do not claim title. We'll provide explicit language that assigns output ownership to Holloway and carves out only a narrow telemetry/feedback license.
- Training: We can accept a training opt-out for raw customer content. Our ask is to retain a scoped feedback license to improve platform performance (e.g., aggregated telemetry, prompt pattern signals) unless a customer opts out. For any use that would involve customer raw content or fine-tuning, we require explicit opt-in.

I'm looping Laura and Grace (legal + product) to draft targeted redlines and SOC2 evidence. Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow (Fri) 11:00am PT to walk through the tweaks? Here is a Calendly link: https://calendly.com/redwood/dev-30

I'll attach a preliminary one-page summary of our proposed edits separately.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Account Lead — Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@hollowayhealth.com>, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, Morgan Blake <morgan.blake@hollowayhealth-legal.com>
Date: Thu, 9 May 2028 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Holloway — MSA/Order Form: proposed redlines (MSA + Order Form)

Sophie / team — attaching tracked-change redlines (Holloway_MSA_Redlines.pdf and Holloway_OrderForm_Redline.docx). Summary of our positions below. FYI Grace, happy to take notes from product.

Summary (Redwood positions):
- Output ownership: Redwood will insert a clear clause: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Outputs generated by Customer Content; Redwood shall have no ownership rights in Outputs." We are comfortable adding language preventing Redwood from assigning or sublicensing Outputs.

- Training / feedback license: two-tier approach we propose:
  * Feedback telemetry: Redwood may use aggregated and de-identified telemetry (usage metrics, token patterns, system performance data) to improve the service. This is expressly non-attributable to customer content.
  * Raw-content training: Redwood will not use Customer Content to train or fine-tune base models without Customer's prior written consent (opt-in). The Order Form can include a checkbox to opt-in to "Model Improvement / Fine-tuning".

- Duration / deletion: we propose that any transient caches or KV state tied to in-flight requests are deleted within 30 days unless retention is required for billing/ops; for opted-in training artifacts we will keep a record of consent and a narrow retention schedule described in Exhibit B.

- Feedback license scope: limited, perpetual (only for aggregated improvements), and non-exclusive; we can further limit to exclude any downstream commercialization of customer outputs.

Please review the attached redlines. If Holloway prefers slightly different wording on the training carveout, point edits are welcome. For SOC2 evidence, see the link in evidence-soc2-link.txt included with this thread.

Next steps: if the edits look acceptable, Dev can push the updated Order Form into DocuSign and we can proceed to signatures.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments:
- Holloway_MSA_Redlines.pdf (summary + tracked changes)
- Holloway_OrderForm_Redline.docx (clean copy with checkboxes for opt-in)
- evidence-soc2-link.txt (link to SOC2 + compliance pack)

From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@hollowayhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@hollowayhealth.com, Morgan Blake <morgan.blake@hollowayhealth-legal.com>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Holloway — MSA/Order Form: proposed redlines (MSA + Order Form)

Laura / Dev — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. I reviewed the summary with our legal team. A few follow-ups before we can sign:

1) Training opt-in: Holloway will likely agree to an opt-in box for fine-tuning, but we need stronger contractual guarantees that any opted-in training will never expose Holloway PII, PHI or patient-identifiable material. We would require Redwood to publish and follow a documented de-identification process and provide evidence that training corpora excludes PHI.

2) Feedback telemetry: we can accept aggregated signals, but please add an explicit prohibition on the use of any prompt/response pairs derived from Holloway content for commercial model releases. Aggregated performance improvements are OK; raw pairs are not.

3) SOC2 / evidence: the link in evidence-soc2-link.txt points to a customer portal that requires an access token. Please send the token, or alternatively attach the SOC2 report and a short summary of third-party attestations.

4) We also want a 12-month data deletion option after contract termination (instead of 30 days) for any operational backups that contain customer content — at minimum, a warranty that such backups will be deleted within 12 months and a process to request earlier deletion.

If you can accept the above and supply the SOC2 evidence, we should be able to move forward. We can do the call tomorrow at 11:00am PT — Sophie / Morgan will join.

Best,
Sophie

Subject: Re: Holloway — MSA/Order Form: final alignment and next steps

Sophie / Morgan — appreciate the detailed feedback; glad we're close. Quick summary of what Redwood will commit to in the final Order Form and Exhibit language: 

1) Output ownership: explicit clause that Holloway retains all rights to Outputs. Redwood will add a negative covenant preventing assignment/sublicense of Outputs.

2) Training / feedback: we accept the following binding controls:
   - No use of raw Customer Content for base-model training or commercial model releases without prior written opt-in.
   - Opt-in flow: the Order Form will include a checkbox to opt-in to "Model Improvement / Fine-tuning". Any opted-in program will require documented de-identification steps; Redwood will provide an outline of the de-identification process and evidence that PHI/PII are excluded from training corpora.
   - Feedback telemetry: allowed for aggregated, non-attributable performance improvements only; no prompt/response pairs from Holloway will be used in any commercial model release.

3) Retention & deletion: Redwood will maintain operational caches for up to 30 days, but long-term backups that could contain customer content will be deleted within 12 months post-termination (or earlier upon request where feasible). We will add an Exhibit B table describing retention timelines.

4) Evidence: Laura has provided a link to our SOC2 package; per Sophie please find an attached PDF copy of the SOC2 summary and a one-page description of our de-id process. (Attachment: SOC2_Summary_Redwood.pdf)

Next steps:
- Laura / Grace: please incorporate the 12-month backup deletion warranty and the explicit "no prompt/response use in commercial releases" language into Exhibit A/B.
- Sophie / Holloway: if that language is acceptable, we'll push the updated Order Form to DocuSign and provide the opt-in checkbox for training.

I'll create the DocuSign package once legal confirms the final language. Thanks all — talk tomorrow on the call.

Best,
Dev Patel
Account Lead — Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Attachment: SOC2_Summary_Redwood.pdf
